description: Tests a single targeted prompt change against the production identification baseline on a variant of the 736 thread fixture (12 subtrees of LG vs MSI ultrawide OLED discussion). The fixture used here is `monitors-thread-736-identification-full-with-affinity.fixture.json` — a clone of the original full fixture with two additions needed to reproduce the production failure conditions for issue 1B: (a) `authorId` populated on every author-bearing node (using `t2_<lowercase-name>` to match Reddit's prefix), (b) a top-level `authorAffinity` block mapping `t2_anurinxx → MSI MPG341CQPX (prior_owner)`. Together these cause `formatAffinityLabel` to emit `[used: MSI MPG341CQPX]` markers on AnurinXx's PLAN comments, which is one of the signals that biased the production identification model toward MSI MPG 341CQPX in subtree 9 (the LG 34GP83A-B / 34GN850 case). The new candidate adds a GUARD clause to STEP 1 § 2: when the comment contains an explicit alphanumeric model token (≥4 chars, ≥1 letter, ≥1 digit), parent-context resolution (path 2.3 — parent CONTEXT, same-author chain, PLAN ancestor, single-cheat-sheet pick) is forbidden. Only paths 2.1 (whole-token-equivalent cheat-sheet match), 2.2 (verbatim emission), or 2.4 (empty) may apply. Anaphoric phrases like 'sister to yours' / 'same as yours' and [used: …] markers on parents are explicitly called out as not overriding an explicit token. 2.1's 'partial name' wording is tightened: substring matches that differ by any suffix/prefix character or generation marker fall through to 2.2. 2.2 adds an alignment rule for picking among textually-similar cheat-sheet entries, preferring the closest exact alignment over the conversation's primary product. Two new examples (c14, c15) demonstrate the guard firing: c14 = 'Ha, I am on a LG 34GP83A-B since 2020. Sister monitor to yours' against an MSI-MPG-341CQPX parent chain (subtree 9 — production currently mis-resolves this as MSI MPG 341CQPX); c15 = 'I literally just received my MSI 341CQP' against an MPG-341CQPX-dominated chain (subtree 5 — production currently snaps this to the X model instead of the 175Hz MAG). Goals: (a) the two failure cases above are correctly resolved by the new candidate; (b) no regression on the 13 existing examples (c0-c13 logic preserved with explicit guard-fires/does-not-fire annotations); (c) judge faithfulness score above the baseline.

expectations.desiredOutcome: Schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema for every subtree. Every PLAN comment receives an entry, even when products is empty. Per-subtree expectations below pin the two key regression cases (subtrees 5 and 9). For all other subtrees the default expectation applies: existing baseline behavior is preserved (anaphoric resolutions in c0/c2/c3/c6 etc. still work because no explicit alphanumeric SKU token is present in those comments, so the new guard does not fire).

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10. (1) faithfulness — every real product reference is surfaced and no products are hallucinated. The two cases that motivated this scenario carry extra weight: a comment that explicitly names 'LG 34GP83A-B' or 'LG 34GN850' must emit that LG product (verbatim is acceptable since they are not in the cheat sheet); a comment that explicitly names 'MSI 341CQP' (no trailing X) must emit MSI MAG 341CQP (not MSI MPG 341CQPX). Silently substituting a parent-chain product (typically MSI MPG 341CQPX) for an explicit token in the body is a faithfulness penalty. Verbatim model preservation continues to count: '34GS9QE' must NOT be silently upgraded to '34GS95QE-B'. (2) calibration — contentQuality matches depth per the schema enum: 'high' = substantive evaluation with specifics, comparison, or detailed first-hand experience; 'medium' = verdict or preference without depth; 'low' = product named but not evaluated. Borderline cases err lower. Variant accuracy (MAG 341CQP at 175Hz vs MPG 341CQPX at 240Hz) counts here too. (3) completeness — every PLAN comment has an entry even when products is empty; jokes, thanks, meta-replies correctly produce empty arrays without inventing products. Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness,calibration,completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'. In the rationale, call out subtree-5 (the 175Hz MSI 341CQP case) and subtree-9 (the LG 34GP83A-B / 34GN850 case) specifically and report what each candidate emitted there.

expectations.desiredOutcome: Cheat sheet has both 'MSI MPG 341CQPX' (240Hz) and 'MSI MAG 341CQP' (175Hz). Subtree contains 'I literally just received my MSI 341CQP the other day, and it's gorgeous...' (Lionhearted72) plus the same author's later clarification 'I have the 175Hz non "X" model, the 341CQP!'. Both comments must resolve to MSI MAG 341CQP, NOT MSI MPG 341CQPX. The trailing 'X' is absent in the comment text — '341CQP' aligns whole-token-equivalent to MAG 341CQP, not to MPG 341CQPX. Production baseline currently mis-resolves the first comment to MSI MPG 341CQPX. The candidate must emit MSI MAG 341CQP for both.

Subtree's parent chain has been discussing 'MSI MPG 341CQPX' for several depths, with [used: MSI MPG341CQPX] markers on the AnurinXx PLAN comments. Two PLAN comments name explicit non-cheat-sheet LG products: AnurinXx's 'So I stayed with my LG 34GN850 until now' and demi9od's reply 'Ha, I am on a LG 34GP83A-B since 2020. Sister monitor to yours.' Both LG products must be surfaced (verbatim emission is correct since neither is in the cheat sheet). The phrase 'Sister monitor to yours' is an anaphor pointing AT the parent's MSI but does NOT relabel the explicit '34GP83A-B' token. Production baseline currently emits MSI MPG 341CQPX for demi9od's comment and drops the 34GN850 entirely. The candidate must emit LG 34GP83A-B for demi9od's comment and LG 34GN850 for AnurinXx's comment.
